By Michael Doyle

Topic:NRL

Isaah Yeo of the Panthers looks on during the round 21 NRL match between Parramatta Eels and Penrith Panthers at Western Sydney Stadium, on July 23, 2026, in Sydney, Australia. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

Penrith captain Isaah Yeo may miss the rest of the NRL season after injuring his pectoral muscle, while the Sydney Roosters joined the Panthers on top of the table after defeating the Canterbury Bulldogs.

Yeo came off in the first half of Penrith's 28-12 loss to the New Zealand Warriors in Auckland on Friday night, with the Auckland-based side solidifying their status as a genuine premiership threat in 2026.

Yeo was clutching his pectoral muscle after reeling out of a tackle, with scans needed to confirm if he has sustained a tear.

Should scans confirm a pectoral tear, he could be out for the rest of the season.

"It doesn't look great," Panthers coach Ivan Cleary said during his press conference.

"Obviously Yeoy's a big loss and hard to replace, but that's how it goes.

"If that's the case, we'll have to (replace him)."

The Roosters have joined the Panthers on 36 points at the top of the NRL ladder, surviving a scare to pip the Bulldogs 20-18.

The Roosters held an 8-2 lead at half-time, but the Bulldogs scored three tries in 11 minutes to take an 18-8 lead with 25 minutes to play.

But two quick tries in the final 15 minutes for the Roosters earned them a hard-fought win.

Meanwhile, Craig Bellamy says he will be coach of the Melbourne Storm in 2027, despite recent health issues.

By Michael Doyle

This is where we end tonight's live blog coverage of the NRL.

The Warriors earned a statement win over the Panthers, while the Roosters were gritty in their victory over the Bulldogs.

Panthers captain Issah Yeo is potentially at risk of missing the rest of the NRL season with a pec injury.

ABC Sport will be back tomorrow to bring you more live coverage of round 23.

We hope you join us then.

Goodnight.

By Michael Doyle

Luke Metcalf was a star for the New Zealand Warriors tonight.

Playing his first NRL match since round five, he scored two tries in the Wahs' 28-12 win over the Penrith Panthers.

Metcalf has been playing NSW Cup in the previous few weeks, and is off to the Dragons next year.

But he got his chance to partner Chanel Harris-Tavita, following an injury to Te Maire Martin.

Tanah Boyd, is another Warriors half who is injured, showcasing the depth the Auckland-based team has in the halves.

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

— reporting by AAP

Isaah Yeo's NRL season appears in doubt after the Penrith co-captain suffered a suspected pectoral injury in a 28-12 loss to the Warriors that blows open the race for the minor premiership.

The talismanic lock and NSW captain pulled up sore after making a tackle and left the field during the final 10 minutes of the first half in Auckland.

If scans confirm a pectoral tear, Yeo could miss the remainder of the Panthers' push for a fifth premiership in six seasons.

"It doesn't look great," Panthers coach Ivan Cleary said of Yeo's injury.

"Obviously Yeoy's a big loss and hard to replace, but that's how it goes, if that's the case, we'll have to (replace him)."

By Michael Doyle

The Bulldogs had a big chance to cause an upset tonight, leading 18-8 over the Roosters with 15 minutes to play.

But two quick tries, with the match-winner coming off a bomb that wasn't contested, allowed the Roosters to snatch a two-point win.

The loss means the Bulldogs will finish this weekend outside the NRL top eight.

Bulldogs centre Matt Burton says there is a lot that his side can take from tonight, but they are disappointed to miss out on a big opportunity.

There was plenty of positives out of it. Just little moments in big games cost you, and I think we missed a few tonight.

We fought hard; just little moments in the game cost us.

By Michael Doyle

Roosters half Daly Cherry-Evans went equal with Cooper Cronk to be second on the all-time first-grade games list, playing his 372nd game tonight.

The Roosters had to fight to get the win over the Bulldogs, and often were their own worst enemy with errors.

But Cherry-Evans tells ABC Sport the Tricolours can be proud of how they overcame the self-inflicted adversity.

That was a close game. We made life really hard for ourselves, and they're a quality opposition. But we should be proud to get the job done.

We could have thrown the towel in, but a real show of resilience from the boys.

By Michael Doyle

Sydney Roosters winger Billy Smith scored two tries in the 20-18 win over the Canterbury Bulldogs.

It was not a pretty win for the Roosters, especially when you consider they scored 82 points last week.

Smith has spoken to ABC Sport, and says the team will be happy to win, despite not producing their best.

"We weren't great, to be completely honest," Smith says.

"Last year, we probably lose those games. Happy with the win."

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

— reporting by AAP

Sydney Roosters have edged past Canterbury in a 20-18 win that has blown the race for the NRL's minor premiership wide open.

On a pivotal night in the make-up of the top four, the Roosters moved up to second with a late win at Allianz Stadium that puts Trent Robinson's men level on 36 points with ladder-leading Penrith.

The Panthers, who sit first as a result of their superior for and against, host the Roosters next Thursday and look set to be without captain Isaah Yeo.

Even without facing Yeo, the Roosters will have to turn things up a notch against the Panthers as the race for the minor premiership looks set to go to the wire.

Robinson's side led 8-2 at halftime on Friday but were stunned when a try from Lachlan Galvin and a Jacob Kiraz double in a 12-minute second-half spell catapulted the Bulldogs into an unlikely lead.

But a miscommunication at the back by Bulldogs fullback Connor Tracey allowed Salesi Foketi to dive on a loose kick and claim the match-winning try in the 69th minute.

The victory gave the Roosters a seventh-straight win but also puts a major dent in Canterbury's top-eight aspirations after they threatened to upset the home side.

Stephen Crichton kicked a penalty to get the Bulldogs on the board after six minutes before Sam Walker and Hugo Savala combined down the left to send Billy Smith in at the corner.

Then after Matt Burton failed to gather a Daly Cherry-Evans bomb, Siua Wong touched down for the Roosters who led 8-2 at half-time after Walker failed to convert both kicks.

The Bulldogs had struggled for spark in the first half but they came back after half-time with a bang as hooker Bailey Hayward burst up the middle of the field and found a supporting Kiraz.

The Canterbury winger scored under the posts as Crichton converted to tie the game up.

Galvin then put the Bulldogs ahead for the first time when the five-eighth drifted across field and darted through a Reece Robson tackle to score.

Galvin set up Kiraz for his side's third, but Canterbury were unable to find a knockout blow and the Roosters clawed their way back into the game.

Smith added a second with 15 minutes left before Foketi was in the right place at the right time, touching down a Walker bomb that Tracey failed to take to score the decisive try.

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

The Bulldogs had the ball on their own 30-metre line.

A pass from Lachlan Galvin was dropped by Stephen Crichton, then picked up by Galvin in an offside position.

The Roosters have decided to kick for goal to try and extend their lead to four points.

From 32 metres out, just to the right of the posts, Sam Walker pulls the kick and misses.

Roosters 20

Bulldogs 18

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

It is an absolute disaster for the Bulldogs.

Sam Walker, on the halfway, puts up a massive bomb.

The ball bounces between three Bulldogs players and bounces into the in-goal.

Roosters second-rower Salesi Foketi chases through, wins the race to the ball, and grounds it with one hand.

Brilliant from Foketi.

From directly in front, Sam Walker kicks the goal and the Roosters hold a two-point lead.

Roosters 20

Bulldogs 18

By Michael Doyle

The Roosters have been threatening the Bulldogs' goal-line for several minutes.

The Tricolours finally found a moment of class, with a shift to the left creating an overlap, and winger Billy Smith touches down in the corner.

From the left touchline, Sam Walker nails the conversion attempt.

Roosters 14

Bulldogs 18

By Michael Doyle

In the first half, the Roosters threw a forward pass off a scrum, 10 metres from the Bulldogs' goal-line.

IN the second half, centre Rob Toia drops the ball off the pass from the scrum, 10 metres from the Bulldogs' goal-line.

By Michael Doyle

The Roosters will be wishing they could carry forward 20 or 30 points from last round...

- Mike

Rooster Sam Walker is being tackled by three Bulldogs, and the ball comes loose.

A knock-on has been called.

Walker demands a challenge, believing the ball went backwards.

It's close, but the Bunker has sided with the Roosters.

By Michael Doyle

Bang. Bang. Bang.

The Bulldogs have scored three tries in 11 minutes to completely change the complexion of this match.

The Roosters were running with the ball from near their own goal-line.

Roosters fullback Cody Ramsey dropped the ball, and the Bulldogs picked it up and threw the ball to right winger Jacob Kiraz.

Kiraz puts the foot down and wins the race to the corner for Canterbury's third try.

Roosters 8

Bulldogs 18

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

The Bulldogs have burst into life.

Halfback Lachlan Galvin threw a dummy, then busted out of a tackle attempt from Rooster Reece Robson, and Galvin scored the try.

The Roosters are giving away the ball too easily, with a poor error on the halfway line giving the Bulldogs the chance to attack the goal-line.

Crichton kicks the goal. and in the blink of an eye, the Bulldogs have a six-point lead.

Roosters 8

Bulldogs 14

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

Outstanding dummy half work from Bulldogs hooker Bailey Hayward.

He scooted out of dummy half and ran through an enormous gap in the Roosters' defence.

Roosters prop Lindsay Collins didn't try to tackle. He must have either thought he was offside, or was called offside by the ref.

Hayward ran 50 metres, then passed to winger Jacob Kiraz who ran the final 25 metres to score under the posts.

Scores are level as Stephen Crichton converts.

Roosters 8

Bulldogs 8

By Michael Doyle

By Michael Doyle

It's bad news for Sitili Tupouniua. He is out with a hamstring issue.

He missed the previous five matches for the Bulldogs with a hamstring injury.

The Roosters enjoy a good set before kicking clear.

The Roosters have scored both of the tries in this match, but Sam Walker has been unable to convert either.

The Bulldogs are in the fight, but lacking the final pass to finish off attacking raids.
